messages.content:
You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE battle (
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT,
    date TEXT,
    bulgarian_commander TEXT,
    latin_commander TEXT,
    result TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id)
);

CREATE TABLE ship (
    lost_in_battle INT,
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT,
    tonnage TEXT,
    ship_type TEXT,
    location TEXT,
    disposition_of_ship TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (lost_in_battle) REFERENCES battle(id)
);

CREATE TABLE death (
    caused_by_ship_id INT,
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    note TEXT,
    killed INT,
    injured INT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (caused_by_ship_id) REFERENCES ship(id)
);

To list the historical battles in your `battle` table, you can start with:

```sql
SELECT
  id,
  name,
  date,
  bulgarian_commander,
  latin_commander,
  result
FROM battle
ORDER BY date, name;
```

If you mean something more specific (e.g., only battles with ships lost, only Bulgarian victories, a date range, etc.), tell me what you want to filter by.
focus on battles where more than 10 people got killed

```sql
SELECT
  b.id,
  b.name,
  b.date,
  b.bulgarian_commander,
  b.latin_commander,
  b.result,
  SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) AS total_killed
FROM battle b
JOIN ship s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
JOIN death d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY
  b.id, b.name, b.date, b.bulgarian_commander, b.latin_commander, b.result
HAVING SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) > 10
ORDER BY total_killed DESC, b.date, b.name;
```
make sure the total deaths across all involved is over 10

```sql
SELECT
  b.id,
  b.name,
  b.date,
  b.bulgarian_commander,
  b.latin_commander,
  b.result,
  SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) AS total_killed
FROM battle b
JOIN ship s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
JOIN death d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY
  b.id, b.name, b.date, b.bulgarian_commander, b.latin_commander, b.result
HAVING SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) > 10
ORDER BY total_killed DESC, b.date, b.name;
```

This sums `death.killed` across all ships linked to the battle (via `ship.lost_in_battle`) and filters to battles where the total is > 10.
also should show battle names with IDs

```sql
SELECT
  b.id AS battle_id,
  b.name AS battle_name,
  SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) AS total_killed
FROM battle b
JOIN ship s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
JOIN death d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.name
HAVING SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) > 10
ORDER BY total_killed DESC, b.id;
```
make sure to include unique identifiers for the battles too.

```sql
SELECT
  b.id AS battle_id,         -- unique identifier
  b.name AS battle_name,
  SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) AS total_killed
FROM battle b
JOIN ship s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
JOIN death d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.name
HAVING SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) > 10
ORDER BY total_killed DESC, b.id;
```
